uncited: This family encompasses the deployment, integration, and hardware acceleration of volume rendering techniques in real-world scenarios.

It addresses the gap between theoretical rendering algorithms and practical implementation constraints, such as computational intensity, display hardware limitations, and user interaction requirements.

It is distinguished from [Image-order rendering](16-image-order-rendering.md) and [Object-order rendering](22-object-order-rendering.md) by its focus on the system-level architecture (e.g., GPU pipelines, web browsers, physical displays) rather than the specific sampling or shading strategies used per pixel or voxel.
The articles in this family share the goal of mapping abstract volumetric data $I(x,y,z)$ to a perceptible output through specific system constraints.

**Hardware Acceleration Mapping**: Offloading computationally intensive tasks (ray casting, splatting, sorting) to parallel execution units (GPUs, multi-core CPUs) to achieve real-time or near-real-time performance [S1, unofficial].

**Data Structure Optimization**: Storing volumetric data in formats optimized for the target hardware, such as 3D/4D textures for coalesced memory access on GPUs or sparse structures (e.g., OpenVDB) for memory efficiency [S1, unofficial].

**Depth Management**: Handling the ordering of contributions for alpha-blended rendering, often requiring GPU-based sorting algorithms (radix sort, linked lists) to ensure correct compositing [S1, unofficial].

**Physical-to-Digital Mapping**: In the case of volumetric displays, transforming 3D voxel coordinates into 2D control signals (pixel buffers, SLM patterns) synchronized with mechanical or optical processes to create a physical 3D light field [S1, unofficial].
Volume rendering has evolved from offline scientific visualization tools to real-time interactive systems and specialized hardware displays.
The integration of GPUs has been a major driver, enabling complex shading and large datasets to be rendered interactively.

More recently, web-based technologies (WebGL/WebGPU) have democratized access to volume visualization, while volumetric displays offer a new paradigm for 3D data presentation without stereoscopic headgear.
